newsitem.title: UK: NWE, US refinery margins rise, mogas surge helps.
newsitem.headline: NWE, US refinery margins rise, mogas surge helps.

text.p: Oil refining margins were mixed last week in most centres. Rotterdam and the U.S. east coast saw gains, while the Med and Far East saw margins continue to slide.

The outlook looked encouraging in Europe and the U.S. where storming gasoline prices, up over $35 a tonne for delivered unleaded premium grade in NWE over the last two weeks, acted as a beacon for battered refiners.
Gasoline's rise higher has been fuelled by cat cracker problems over the weekend at three Northwest European refineries, the continued strength of MTBE and a fundamental shortage of European product.

Average margins for complex cracking refiners in the key European Rotterdam area running Brent crude rose to $1.95 a barrel at the end of last week compared with $1.41 the previous week, according to Reuters data calculated from standard product yields.

Margins in U.S. Gulf Coast refineries running Brent crude rose to $1.94 from $1.30 a week previous. Although the rise was substantial it was a few cents off the $2.52 seen on July 30, the middle of last week.
In all the other areas the picture was less rosy as margins fell.

The Mediterranean was worst hit as the spectre of Iraqi crude arriving neared. Last week simple hyrdo-skimming units running Urals crude oil saw margins of 41 cents in the red compared with -14 cents a week earlier.
Margins have been sliding in the Mediterranean since the end of July when hydro-skimmers were showing a margin of +94 cents.
Margins for complex cracking refineries in Singapore running Dubai crude fell to $1.74 from $2.06.
Poor regional demand for light distillates has depressed prices and the immediate prospects did not look good given current high stocks in north Asia.
